name: No-Boil Chicken Pasta Casserole with Artichokes and Peas

ingredients.buy: 12 oz (2 1/3 of the 5.2 oz packages), crumbled
1 lb 4 oz drained (about 2 1/3 cans), roughly chopped
2 1/3 tsp finely grated (zest of the same lemons)

prose.intro_html:
Here is the deal with dump-and-bake casseroles. They promise dinner with almost no work, and most of them hand you back a pan of mush. This one does not. No-Boil Chicken Pasta Casserole with Artichokes and Peas leans on a creamy blender sauce, lean chicken breast, and a little brightness from lemon and artichoke to keep a week of lunches from getting boring.

The math is what sells me. Every container lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein, and you never boiled a single pot of pasta. The dry penne cooks right in the sauce while the oven does the work. That is the kind of shortcut I can get behind.
prose.shop_smart:
• Penne is the backbone here, and you need 1 lb 12 oz of dry pasta. Standard boxes run 1 lb, so pick up two and set the leftover aside for another night.
  • Chicken breast is 3 1/2 lb, cut into 1-inch cubes. A family pack saves you the trimming and gives you clean, even pieces that cook at the same rate.
  • Boursin Garlic and Fine Herbs comes in 5.2 oz packages, and you need about 2 1/3 of them, so grab three. What you do not use keeps well for spreading on crackers later in the week.
  • Get plain canned artichoke hearts, not the marinated kind packed in oil. You want 1 lb 4 oz drained, which is roughly 2 1/3 cans. Drain them hard and give them a rough chop.
  • Frozen green peas go in straight from the bag with no thawing. You need 2 1/3 cups.
  • Cottage cheese carries the sauce and parmesan builds the top. Any fat level of cottage cheese blends smooth, so grab the container that fits your cart.
prose.make_it:
The whole trick is that nothing gets pre-cooked. You build the sauce, you dump the rest in, and the oven finishes the job.

  1. Heat the oven to 400 degrees F and lightly grease a 9x13 casserole dish. Scaling to the full 14 servings means splitting across two dishes or one deep pan.
  2. Build the sauce in a blender or food processor. Add the cottage cheese, crumbled Boursin, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt, and blend until smooth. Pour in the chicken broth and blend again until it is completely smooth. It will look very thin, and that is exactly right, because the pasta is going to drink it up.
  3. Layer the dish. Dry penne on the bottom, then scatter the cubed chicken, the peas, and the chopped artichoke hearts over the top. Pour the sauce over everything and press down so every piece of pasta is submerged.
  4. Cover tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Pull it, take off the foil, and give it a good stir. The pasta should still be a touch undercooked here. Top with the parmesan and return it to the oven for another 5 to 10 minutes, bumping the heat a little if you want a golden top. If it already feels done, add the parmesan and skip the extra time.
  5. Let it rest at least 10 minutes so the sauce sets up. Finish with chopped fresh parsley or basil and serve.
prose.portion_html:
Fourteen servings means you portion by weight, not by eyeball. Weigh your empty dish before you cook and note that number, or weigh the finished casserole and subtract the pan. Take the total food weight, divide by 14, and that is your target grams per container.

Scoop to that number and you get 14 honest servings that each hit {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein. Casserole settles as it cools, so a scale keeps the last container as full as the first. Stir the peas and artichoke through as you portion so every box gets its share instead of one lucky lid getting all the good stuff.
prose.cost_closing_html: Here is where it pays off. A tray of chicken, pasta, artichoke, and three kinds of cheese lands at ${{cost_ps}} per serving. That is a scratch-made dinner carrying {{protein}} grams of protein for less than most drive-through combos, and you cooked 14 of them in one shot. Cook once, eat all week, and let the oven do the labor.

head.description: A no-boil chicken pasta casserole with artichokes and peas that dumps and bakes in one dish. Fourteen high-protein meal-prep servings with a creamy Boursin cottage cheese sauce.
head.keywords: no boil chicken pasta casserole, dump and bake casserole, chicken artichoke pasta bake, high protein meal prep dinner, Boursin cottage cheese pasta, budget meal prep chicken casserole
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F and lightly grease a 9x13 casserole dish.
Blend the cottage cheese, crumbled Boursin, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt until smooth, then blend in the chicken broth until the sauce is thin and completely smooth.
Place the dry penne in the dish, then scatter the cubed chicken, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts over the pasta.
Pour the blended sauce over everything, pressing the pasta down until it is fully submerged.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes.
Remove the foil, stir well, top with grated parmesan, and bake another 5 to 10 minutes until golden.
Rest at least 10 minutes, then garnish with chopped fresh parsley or basil and serve.
